title: xtask: the heavy gate reaches too many targets for a small diff

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

labels.name: effort:high
labels.description: Several crates, new behaviour with tests; safety floor (issue-worker-high)

labels.name: P5
labels.description: Agent surface and tooling keep up with what shipped

body:
The heavy reach is too coarse. A small diff selects the whole heavy lane of a crate. A run takes 40 to 60 minutes and runs targets that the diff cannot break.

## The decision

The maintainer decided on 2026-11-22 to narrow the reached set. Run only the heavy targets that the changed files touch. Name the other targets "not run" in the review.

## Evidence

- The heavy run of PR #3510 on head `dbe37ad2c`: 207 steps, 0 failed, 42.9 minutes.
- The heavy run of PR #3471 on head `532d0fa92`: 207 steps, 0 failed, 55.8 minutes.

Both changes are small.

## What to change

The heavy mapper in `xtask` maps a changed crate to the whole heavy lane of that crate. It must map a changed file to the heavy test targets that depend on that file. Keep the crate dependency reach as the fallback. Do not reach a test target that does not load the module of the changed file. Print the reason for each reached target and each skipped target in `--dry-run`. Print the count of reached and skipped targets in the run output.

## Open questions

- Which seam gives a safe map: the file path, the `use` graph, or the gate map of each test?
- Does a wide change still select the full lane?
- Does the map handle a change to a test file itself?

## Related

- #3556 and #3558: at review, targeted tests, and the full heavy lanes only at the cut.
- #3320: the heavy gate on main since v0.25.0 is incomplete.
- #3460: the heavy-wave form.
